criteria.name: Introduction — Identifies ethical issues and broad links to engineering design; discusses the context of ethical issues in engineering organisations; identifies relevant stakeholders when considering the ethical issues.
criteria.reasoning: Several issues identified linked to design: quality-safety vs business success. Context of competitive tech industry and stakeholder list demonstrated, but significance and design link remain generic, not excellent depth.

criteria.name: Balanced Discussion — Discusses objective arguments for and against decisions on the ethical issues; draws a conclusion on how stakeholders should make decisions about the issues.
criteria.reasoning: Presents for and against arguments and concludes Not Ship. For-ship arguments speculative and shallow, e.g., competitors will ship anyway, grow to improve. Conclusion focuses on Rachel only, not decisions for several stakeholders.

criteria.name: Report Structure, Format and Language — The report includes appropriate sections serving their functions (abstract, introduction, body, and conclusion); maps, figures, tables, and visual elements are correctly used to support discussion; writing is grammatically correct, fluent, concise, easy to read and understand, and uses appropriate word choice; references are well-structured and appropriate, supporting the report’s motivations.
criteria.reasoning: No abstract despite requirement, no figures or tables or visual elements. Generally fluent but typos and spacing errors and poorly formatted references. Sections present but abstract omission is major structural failure.

technical_issues.where: DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship
technical_issues.issue: States 1% of 5,000 servers = 500 failed servers; correct is 50. Quantitative error undermines risk assessment.
States Volkswagen installed defeat devices in electric vehicles to manipulate crash-safety tests; correct was diesel vehicles to manipulate emissions tests.

overall: Balanced for/against with relevant cases supports Not Ship, but maths and VW factual errors, missing abstract and visuals, and thin stakeholder coverage limit marks.

feedback.summary: You made a clear case for Not Ship with relevant NHS and EACE evidence and logical for/against structure. To improve, you need to correct your 1% calculation and VW facts, add abstract and visuals, and extend decisions to all stakeholders with deeper design links.
next_steps: Correct your errors in DICUSSION and The Most Ethical Path: change 500 to 50 servers for 1% of 5,000 and rewrite VW as diesel emissions defeat devices.
Add a concise abstract and one visual such as a stakeholder-risk table, then proofread your DICUSSION heading, spacing and References formatting.
Deepen your for-ship case with objective evidence and write distinct ship/not-ship recommendations for Rachel, her company, chip supplier and health department.

criteria.C1: You identified quality-safety vs business success in INTRODUCTION and listed Rachel, company, chip supplier and health department. For Excellent you need to explain significance for engineering design and show deeper understanding of both organisational context and stakeholder interests.
criteria.C2: You structured for/against in DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship to support Not Ship in The Most Ethical Path. For Very good you need deeper objective evidence for ship arguments beyond competitors will ship anyway and link conclusions to decision-making.
criteria.C3: You built logical for, against, synthesis in CONCLUSION that Not Ship is the most ethical path with sound harm/integrity understanding. For Excellent you need systematic coverage of all stakeholders, especially the chip company, with structure fully supporting your conclusion.
criteria.C4: You used NHS record failures in The Most Ethical Path and EACE code well. For Very good you must correct 1% of 5,000 to 50 in DICUSSION and VW to diesel-emissions, and strengthen quantitative evidence with accurate relevant references.
criteria.C5: You kept sections fluent despite typo in DICUSSION heading. For Good you need to add the missing abstract, include at least one figure/table, and proofread spacing and format References consistently.
